sam_irving: Noticed a weird one: users removed by SCIM are still listed as members in our RBAC table and can access dedicated clusters.

lina-chen: oh — are they removed in Okta but still present in Redwood UI?

sam_irving: Yes. Okta shows deprovisioned. SCIM logs show 200 for the Delete, but audit shows a subsequent `membership.add` event from the provisioning-worker.

rajiv-singh: that smells like a race between the SCIM deprovision flow and our JIT SSO sync. Any timestamps?

sam_irving: SCIM delete at 2025-11-06T17:12:03Z. provisioning-worker re-add at 2025-11-06T17:12:05Z (2s later).

kate-morris: provisioning-worker version? we reverted something last week I think.

sam_irving: release/2025-10-29 build. provisioning-worker logs attached via scim-bot.

scim-bot: Attached: /var/log/provisioning/worker-2025-11-06.log (snippet)

scim-bot: ```
INFO 17:12:03 scim: PATCH /Users/123 -> 200 OK
INFO 17:12:05 prov-worker: user 123 reconcile -> added group 'engineers' (source=login-sso)
ERROR 17:12:06 prov-worker: conflict detected but fallback applied
```

lina-chen: So SCIM says delete, prov-worker sees a login event and re-applies groups via the SSO mapping. That would reintroduce membership despite SCIM intent.

rajiv-singh: We have two sources of truth: SCIM provisioning and JIT mapping. We didn't implement a last-write winner. Need to treat SCIM delete as authoritative for at least X minutes after deprov.

kate-morris: Can we quick-block: when SCIM delete for a user occurs, set a tombstone flag `scim_deprovisioned_at` in users table. Have JIT ignore users with tombstone < TTL.

sam_irving: I wrote a quick query to find affected users:

sam_irving: ```sql
SELECT u.id, u.email, u.scim_deprovisioned_at, r.role
FROM users u
JOIN user_roles r ON r.user_id = u.id
WHERE u.scim_deprovisioned_at IS NOT NULL AND u.active_session_count > 0;
```

lina-chen: nice. I ran it and found 18 users, 3 with admin-ish roles.

security-scan-bot: Security alert: 3 deprovisioned users still have elevated roles. Ticket created in SecOps: SEC-2025-442.

ops-incident-bot: Incident INC-2025-0812 opened for persistent access after deprovision.

rajiv-singh: Action items: (1) emergency migration to add `scim_deprovisioned_at` tombstones from historical SCIM logs, (2) patch prov-worker to ignore JIT mapping if tombstone within 30d, (3) run reconciliation job to strip roles for tombstoned users with no active account. I'll own (2).

kate-morris: I'll take (1) and coordinate DB migration. Sam, can you run a safety script to revoke elevated roles for users flagged?

sam_irving: On it. Running dry-run first. Command I used: `python tools/revoke_roles.py --filter scim_deprovisioned`

lina-chen: After patch, let's also add an audit-rule that any `role.add` within 10s of `scim.delete` gets flagged for manual review.

rajiv-singh: Agreed. Also need a unit test for the race: mock SCIM delete + SSO login events and assert prov-worker respects tombstone.

kate-morris: FYI, compliance wants a note for GDPR dataflow: deprovision means access removed ASAP. We'll need to include timeline in postmortem.

sam_irving: I'll paste results after dry-run (should be quick).

sam_irving: dry-run output: `would_revoke=18, elevated_revoke=3`

lina-chen: OK deploy plan: patch prov-worker + add tombstone column + reconcile job -> deploy to staging, smoke test with synthetic SCIM delete events.

rajiv-singh: timeline: I'll have a prov-worker PR by EOD, tests included. Kate/Lina handle DB and recon. Sam will run the revocation after staging sign-off.

ops-incident-bot: INC-2025-0812 updated: mitigation in progress, ETA 3h.

sam_irving: Thanks all. Will follow up with logs + ops runbook snippets.`
